title: Organizational Verification Policy Document
description: An org-declarable set of EXECUTABLE verification-policy rules (dv_harness/org_verification_policy_engine.py). Each policy is DATA -- a condition over project facts plus an action to take when it matches -- never Python code. Precedence between conflicting policies is resolved by ORG_POLICY_PRECEDENCE_ORDER in the engine, never by which one happened to load last.

scope.description: Who declared this policy. 'org' outranks 'project' in the documented precedence order, unless overridable_by_project is true.

severity.description: MANDATORY outranks ADVISORY as the final precedence tiebreaker; it does not by itself change action_if_matched's meaning.

precedence.description: Explicit numeric precedence, higher wins, within a tied scope. Never required -- an undeclared value is treated as 0, never as an unfair advantage or disadvantage nobody chose.

overridable_by_project.description: Only meaningful when scope is 'org'. True means this org policy explicitly yields to a matching project-scope policy on the same 'governs' topic, ranked below every project policy rather than above it.

governs.description: The named topic/fact this policy is about. Two matched policies sharing one governs value with different action_if_matched values are a real conflict, resolved by precedence or reported unresolved -- never silently averaged.

citation.description: Where this policy comes from (a standards document, a prior incident, an org directive) -- optional, but recorded verbatim when present rather than paraphrased.

condition.description: A three-valued (True/False/UNRESOLVABLE) boolean expression over project facts. A leaf names one fact and an operator; all_of/any_of/not compose leaves. Recursive.

fact.description: Dotted path into the supplied facts mapping, e.g. 'waiver.status'.

value.description: Required for every op except exists/not_exists.
